title: Decision: mimid-agent's default member role gets canRemoveOwnClient, so a did_webvh revocation Commit passes room policy
description:
draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-01 §Revoking a Device: a remaining device of the user commits the new log "together with Remove proposals for the revoked device's leaves"; §Rules make the Remove mandatory. In MIMI the hub then applies room policy (room-policy-04 §8.1.2): removing one's own client without leaving needs canRemoveOwnClient. mimid-agent's default "member" role (crates/mimid-agent-core/src/agent.rs default_roles) did not hold it, so in a room made by mimid-agent a revocation Commit was refused by the hub and the revoked device stayed.

Readings: (a) give the default member role canRemoveOwnClient, so a user can remove their own devices, revoked or not. (b) have the hub authorize, without any capability, a Remove that the did_webvh rules require (the removed leaf's key is not in the record the same Commit sets for its own SCID, and the committer has that SCID). (c) both.

Chosen: (a) now; (b) filed as follow-up (it needs the Observer to say which Removes the rules required). (a) changes only rooms created from now on; existing rooms keep their roles_list, and in them a revocation needs a role change first. Removing one's own other device is an ordinary room-policy capability, and the draft makes it the revocation mechanism, so a messenger room that supports multiple devices needs it.
